chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Uqba, from his father, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed a chest to a man, and there was money in the chest. The heirs said, 'You only have the chest, and you do not have what is inside it.' He said, 'The chest with what is inside it is for him.'

key_terms.صُنْدُوق: Chest or box, a container for valuables

ai.seo_question: Does a bequest of a chest include the money inside it according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of *al-‘ibrah bi-l-‘umum al-murid* (considering the general intent of the bequeather) in cases of ambiguous bequests. This ruling is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for resolving disputes where heirs attempt to limit the gift to the container alone, affirming that the primary intent is the transfer of the item's utility and contents. It underscores the legal maxim that specific items mentioned in a will are presumed to include their inherent contents unless explicitly excluded.
